_about: TRANSLATOR SHELF: Sir Richard Francis Burton (1821-1890) as translator. The Book of the Thousand Nights and a Night (1885, 10 vols) and Supplemental Nights (1886-88, 6 vols) from the Distributed Proofreaders PG editions; Camoens' Lusiads (1880); the Lyricks (1884, 2 parts) from scans of the original printing (round 139). PD. Burton's annotations are famously explicit; they are part of the text as published. Added 2026-10-02 at the coordinator's relay; Adam may veto the whole shelf. No uids minted in the relay burst. Round 139 (2026-10-23) also added The Lands of Cazembe (1873) and Manuel de Moraes (1886, with Isabel Burton).

_excluded.pg-3435..3450: Older PG transcriptions of the same Nights and Supplemental Nights; the DP proofread editions (51252..64384) are used.
_excluded.pg-6036: The Kasidah: Burton's own poem presented as a translation (a literary mask).
_excluded.travel-books: Pilgrimage to Al-Madinah, Lake Regions, etc.: his own prose, not translations (an author section would hold them).
_excluded.pg-27827: The Kama Sutra (Burton and Bhide, 1883): left off by judgment, not rights, like the Pauls' sexology titles. Adam can ask for it.
_excluded.burton-camoens-lyricks-cornell: The Cornell replacement-volume photocopy of the Lyricks (cu31924102142985, 2005) is not used: round 139 found scans of the 1884 Quaritch printing (Toronto Part I, Asiatic Society of Mumbai Part II).

_name_words_note: Translator name(s) only: fetch_shelf.py treats these as the identity check (one must appear in the fetched text), so the original author's name is deliberately NOT listed.

_verified_note: Evidence that each source's rights/identity line was read (lane C review fix, 2026-10-02, pipeline run over the fetched files; no book text recorded). PG: the header's Translator: line and the COPYRIGHTED marker. IA: whether the translator's name appears in the first 30 KB of OCR, and the years printed in the first 15 KB of front matter (scanner/digitizer lines skipped). Any post-1930 year there was examined by eye; see the title's scan_edition.
_surname_note: Full-name phrases, not the bare surname: the bare word ('rose', 'sale', 'lane', 'guest' ...) matches ordinary English (second review round, 2026-10-03).
